findings.text: The frozen prefix set is not literally a message prefix for clauses 3-6: their message literals begin with the fixture-id placeholder, while the frozen prefixes begin at `: `.  A battery implementing `message.startswith(prefix)` on the template binds 0 of those four; a battery implementing it on the rendered message binds 0 as well, because the message begins with the fixture id.  The only consistent reading is 'prefix of the literal text after the leading `{...}` placeholder'.  Both seats must implement that reading identically or R80-C3's rows/bound numbers diverge without either being wrong.

Attack B lands: eight source-text assertions satisfy every frozen count (rows 9, bound 9, survivors 0, pristine 37/0) and even cross-mutant exclusivity.  The predicate never inspects what a case observes.  Fix: also run the condition-disabled mutant per clause and require the declared case to go red there (demonstrated: 8 of 8 vacuous cases stay green).

Attack C lands: a single pristine-green, all-mutant-failing case declared in all nine rows scores bound 9 / survivors 0 / pristine 37/0.  The frozen rule never requires nine distinct cases nor cross-mutant exclusivity.  Fix: require `len(set(declared_cases)) == 9` and, per clause, the declared case to pass on the other eight mutants.

Attack A (a prefix that matches two clauses) is caught only under a total-match + bijection implementation (bound 8); a first-match implementation scores bound 9 with no issue.  Make ambiguity an explicit receipt defect.
Attack D (merged clause) is caught by `guards 9` and by the frozen empty-set kill rule, provided the receipt re-derives the guard list from the source.

`tools/round-80/guard-battery.py` is absent at my check, so `target_pin.matched` and the battery's own `--validate` are unverified here; this seat verifies the inputs those fields must consume (nine guards, nine rows, nine isolating cases, pristine 37/0).

ExecGate's `selftest-pristine.json` names `tools/round-78/attack-gate.py` with the candidate digest df6fb856...; that receipt is provenance-true only after the candidate lands at that path.  It must not be filed into `l1/scores/` before the gate lands (R80-C2's class).

method.candidate_scoring: same enumeration and mutation applied to the candidate blob, plus a table-block parser that binds each row to exactly one clause by the frozen prefix and reads the case name from the fourth cell.
method.clauses: ast.parse of the blob at the rev; Expr(Call(Attribute(Name('defects'),'append'))) inside validate_receipt; literal text from the first argument; enclosing condition read from the source.
method.deletion: one copy per clause with that statement replaced by `pass`; python3 -I -B <copy> --selftest; child env exactly {PATH,HOME,TMPDIR,LANG}; failing cases read from the case JSON lines.
method.discriminator: per clause, replace the enclosing `if` test with False while leaving the message literal in the file; a behavioural case must go red, a source-text case stays green.
